blocks.x: Cyber & Zero-Trust applied to Reinsurance & Commercial Lines. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

Reinsurance and specialty commercial books trade in complexity: treaty structures, cat exposure, bordereaux reconciliation and capital optimization. The data flows between cedants, reinsurers and brokers are still largely spreadsheets — which is why settlement cycles and model confidence suffer.

items: Sensitive exposure data exchanged by email/portal; confidentiality depends on culture.
Ceded premium/loss bordereaux arrive in formats and qualities; reconciliation consumes analysts and hides data quality issues.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Identity & Access Modernization, Cloud Security & Posture Management, Compliance, Audit & Digital Trust from the Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Bordereaux intake/reconciliation, Treaty settlement, Retro/capacity optimization) on Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass. Governance inherits the sector frame — Solvency II / RBC among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Assume breach, plan recovery: resilience engineered, rehearsed and measured.
Evidence once, audit anywhere: compliance automation across SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, DORA and privacy.
Never trust, always verify: zero-trust as an executable architecture, not a slide.
Secured data exchange with counterparties under policy (confidentiality engineered)

blocks.caption: Regimes shaping this capability
rows: reserving, capital and model governance under supervisory review

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Insurance & Risk level this capability reads as: classification-aware DLP, encryption policy and access analytics across health/financial stores (breach-surface measurable and shrinking). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Delivery follows the same weekly rhythm on every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
